title: Zonal Reserved Pools, Cross-AZ Burst Safeguards, and Autoscale SLOs (PRD)
creator: Aja Thompson
description: PRD for zonal-reserved capacity pools, cross-AZ burst safeguard policies, and predictable autoscale SLOs for Redwood Dedicated customers. This spec defines requirements, UX/API design, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, monitoring, and operational runbooks. Goal is to increase predictability of capacity for tenants that require low-latency, region-aware isolation while enabling controlled soft-burst behavior and autoscale guarantees.
background: Customers on Redwood Dedicated ask for more granular reservation and burst controls tied to availability zones (AZs) to improve latency predictability and cost accounting. Current reserved pools are region-wide and do not provide explicit cross-AZ fallback semantics, which causes noisy neighbor effects and unpredictable variance during zone-level disturbances. Additionally, engineering and SRE teams want a bounded autoscale SLO that guarantees a warm buffer and controlled preemption/eviction behavior for reserved tenants.
goals: 1) Introduce zonal-reserved pools so tenants can reserve capacity in specific AZs. 2) Define cross-AZ burst safeguard policies that allow controlled transient bursting with automatic, latency-aware fallback. 3) Provide autoscale SLOs (warm buffer + provisioning time budget) with clear failure modes and operational runbook. 4) Expose controls in API and Console for setting zone preferences, burst budgets, and eviction grace windows.
non_goals: 1) Replacing region-wide reservation model entirely — region-level pools remain supported. 2) Full tenant migration automation from existing reservations (migration tooling may be follow-up). 3) Changes to low-level kernel/runtime scheduling beyond policy layer (runtime optimizations to be coordinated but treated as separate engineering work).
user_stories: As a Platform Engineer, I want to reserve capacity in us-west2-a separately from us-west2-b so our latency-sensitive inference jobs target the closest AZ.
As a SRE, I want guaranteed autoscale SLOs (e.g., 95% of bursts accommodated within 45s) so we can sign SLAs with customers and reduce pager noise.
As a Product Owner, I want to allow customers controlled soft-burst windows (e.g., 5 minutes of 150% capacity) with clear billing and preemption rules.
As an Operator, I want playbooks and alerts for cross-AZ degradation and automatic fallback events so we can respond quickly and inform customers.
As a Customer Admin, I want console controls to set zone affinity, burst allowance, and eviction sensitivity for each reserved pool.
requirements: R1: Zonal Reserved Pools - API and Console support to create reserved pools scoped to a specific AZ (region:us-west2, zone:us-west2-a). Pools must support capacity units and optional soft_burst_budget parameter.

R2: Cross-AZ Burst Safeguards - Policy engine must support configurable fallback order: PREFERRED_ZONE -> PAIRED_ZONE -> REGION_FALLBACK. Fallback must be latency-aware: do not route to fallback if estimated p99 latency will exceed pool SLA threshold.

R3: Burst Budgets - Each reserved pool may define a burst window (duration and multiplier) and a budget quota (tokens per rolling window). Overages must trigger controlled rejections or billed overage according to tenant settings.

R4: Autoscale SLO - Platform guarantees a warm buffer and provisioning time target. Default SLO: 95% of scale-ups for reserved pools accommodated within 45 seconds; p99 within 120 seconds. SLO should be configurable at pool creation (enterprise only).

R5: Eviction & Preemption Controls - Pools expose eviction_sensitivity: {low, medium, high}. High sensitivity prevents preemptions for headroom-critical tenants; low allows faster reclamation under pressure. Preemption logic must honor tenant priority and isolation class.
R6: Observability - Console and API must show token-level cost, per-pool utilization, burst consumption, failed-burst-events, fallback invocations, and provisioning latency histograms.
R7: Audit & RBAC - All pool changes and policy toggles must be logged. RBAC: only admins or specific roles can alter burst budgets and eviction sensitivity.

R8: Backwards Compatibility - Existing region-level reserved pools remain functional; creating zonal pools should not change billing semantics for region pools unless customer opts-in to zone affinity.

R9: Safety Limits - Default global tenant protections: maximum automatic soft-burst multiplier = 2.0 and maximum default burst window = 10 minutes unless explicitly requested and approved by sales/CS.
R10: Billing & Metering - Metering system must attribute burst usage separately and expose forecasted overage to Console before billing cycle end.
api_changes: New endpoints: POST /dedicated/pools (zone optional), PATCH /dedicated/pools/:id (add burst_budget, eviction_sensitivity, zone_affinity), GET /dedicated/pools/:id/metrics. New query params for route selection: preferred_zone and allow_cross_az_fallback. Response schemas include burstBudget, evictSensitivity, zoneAffinity, and autoscaleSLO fields.
console_changes: Console: Pool creation wizard adds 'Zone affinity' dropdown, 'Burst allowance' sliders (duration, multiplier), and 'Eviction sensitivity' radio. Pool detail page adds a Burst consumption timeline, Fallbacks log with root cause links, and a 'Simulate burst' tool for customers to run a dry-run capacity check. Admins get an approval workflow for raising default safety limits.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create a zonal pool in us-east1-b with 50 capacity units and burst window 300s/1.5x. Console and API reflect the pool and fields correctly.

AC2: When preferred_zone is exhausted, system still allows up to burst multiplier in paired zone within budget and records a fallback event. Fallback does not occur if predicted p99 > configured latency threshold.
AC3: Autoscale SLO verification: in controlled load test, 95% of scale-ups are provisioned within 45s and p99 under 120s for a sample pool. Telemetry and dashboards surface this data.
AC4: Eviction sensitivity honored: pool with high sensitivity must not be preempted for 10 minutes after scheduling unless system capacity is in critical overload (defined as >95% cluster fill).
AC5: Billing shows burst usage attribution separate from base reserved consumption for the billing period in both Console and API export.
AC6: RBAC: users without the "PoolAdmin" role cannot change burst budgets or eviction sensitivity via API or Console; attempts must return 403 and be logged.
AC7: Simulated cross-AZ failover produces event in Fallbacks log with expected route and latency estimate; incident runbook is linkable from the log entry.
AC8: Load test that intentionally exceeds safety defaults is rejected or flagged for approval when a customer requests >2x burst multiplier.
metrics: M1: Provisioning latency - time from scale decision to capacity ready (p50/p95/p99) per pool
M2: Burst utilization - percentage of burst budget consumed per pool per rolling 24h
M3: Fallback rate - % of requests routed to non-preferred zone during burst
M4: Preemption events - count and percentage per pool (and correlation with cluster fill)
M5: Customer impact - latency regressions correlated with fallback/preemption events
M6: Billing delta - burst vs reserved spend ratio per tenant
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): implement API and backend policy simulation, run internal teams' workloads and targeted chaos tests (2 weeks). Phase 2 (beta): invite 3 strategic Dedicated customers to opt-in zonal pools and burst safeties; collect telemetry and SLO adherence (6 weeks). Phase 3 (general availability): enable Console controls, add billing attribution, and open opt-in for all customers (4 weeks). Each phase gated by SLO verification, safety test pass, and playbook completion.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: per-pool provisioning latency, burst budget burn-down, fallback log. Alerts: P0 alert when p99 provisioning latency >120s for >15m for any reserved pool; P1 alert when fallback rate >5% sustained for 30m; P2 when burst budget >90% consumed. Alerts route to Platform SRE and dedicated customer success for opted-in accounts.
security_and_compliance: All pool metadata changes audited to internal logging (immutable). RBAC controls must integrate with existing SSO groups. For Private/VPC deployments, zonal affinity must respect network topology and not bypass tenant network isolation. No customer data is moved during fallback; only routing decisions change.
notes:
- Product should coordinate with Sales/CS to define approval workflow for customers requesting >default safety limits.
- Engineering to provide simulation harness for acceptance tests.
- Run expanded chaos testing with single-zone failure to validate graceful degradation and fallback logging.
- Consider later work to enable automatic recommendation of zone affinity based on observed latency distributions.
